method_note: WebFetch failed (DNS ENOTFOUND for every host) in this container, so facts come from WebSearch result snippets and search-engine summaries, not from reading full source documents. The Wikimedia Commons API (read-only, via the agent proxy) was used only to verify image URLs, licences and authors. Image thumbnails could not be downloaded, so the images were not checked visually. The session web-search budget (200) ran out before every topic was covered. Treat 'medium' and 'low' items as needing a check against the primary document.

summary: Tindlu (Thindlu, village code 625674) is a small Hosakote-taluk village of 513 people in 104 households (Census 2011), apparently under Khajihosahalli GP. Directories list a separate 'Thindlu Plantation' village (625673, about 0.97 sq km, no population) next to it, which is the most likely identity of the FOREST block south of the site; its legal forest status still needs checking with the Forest Department. The Hoskote LPA was declared in March 2006, and the BMRDA-prepared Hoskote Planning Authority Master Plan 2031 covers 591.72 sq km and 316 villages. Its approval GO, the agricultural-zone FAR, coverage and setbacks, and the W.P. 4188/2016 status could not be confirmed from accessible sources. Agricultural land needs DC conversion before layout sanction, and BMRDA practice limits agricultural plots to ancillary farmhouses. The STRR stretch next to the site is most likely the ~21 km, 6-lane Hoskote-Tamil Nadu border section (11 m median, 11 underpasses, ROB at Lingadheeramallasandra). Unlike the Dobbaspete-Hoskote section (opened 11 March 2024, tolled from Nov 2023), it was still not confirmed open as of Oct 2026, and the STRR Planning Authority remains a proposal that has not been confirmed as notified. Groundwater is the key environmental constraint: Hoskote is classed over-exploited and notified under the Karnataka Ground Water Act (borewell permission needed), Bengaluru Rural district extraction is about 147%, and the aquifers are weathered and fractured granite-gneiss. Rainfall normal is 813 mm/yr (peak October ~181 mm, bimodal SW and NE monsoons), soils are red sandy clay loam (Ferric Lixisol, 'Hoskote series'), the seismic zone is II, and drainage runs to the South Pennar (Dakshina Pinakini) basin. Growth drivers nearby are Volvo's Rs 1,400 cr Hoskote expansion, warehousing parks (Welspun One 51 acres, Ascendas-Firstspace 91 acres) and the STRR, with asking prices near the STRR at about Rs 3-4 cr/acre for agricultural land (listings, not registered values).
